exercises.prompt: A man builds a rectangular house, and every one of its four walls has a window facing south. A bear walks past the house. What colour is the bear?
exercises.explanation: A house where every wall faces south can only stand at the North Pole. The only bears there are polar bears, so the bear is white.

exercises.prompt: Pulley A is joined to pulley B by a belt crossed in a figure-8. Pulley B is joined to pulley C by an ordinary belt that is not crossed. If A turns clockwise, which way does C turn?
choices: It cannot turn — the system jams
It depends on the pulley sizes
exercises.explanation: A crossed belt reverses the direction of rotation, so B turns counterclockwise. An uncrossed belt keeps the direction, so C also turns counterclockwise.

exercises.prompt: House rule: "The alarm sounds unless the correct code is entered." The rule is always obeyed. Tonight, someone opened the door and the alarm did not sound. What must be true?
exercises.explanation: "A unless B" means "if not B, then A". Here: if the code isn't entered, the alarm sounds. The alarm didn't sound, so by the contrapositive (modus tollens), the code was entered.

exercises.prompt: Which ONE of these groups of statements could all be true at the same time?
choices: Ben is taller than Cy. Cy is taller than Dee. Dee is taller than Ben.
No pets can fly. Some birds are pets. All birds can fly.
Some birds cannot fly. All penguins are birds. No penguin can fly.
Every guest is older than Ann. Ann is a guest.
exercises.answer: Some birds cannot fly. All penguins are birds. No penguin can fly.
exercises.explanation: Penguins can be the birds that can't fly, so nothing clashes. The others contradict themselves: the taller-than chain loops back on itself, the birds that are pets would be flying pets, and Ann can't be older than herself.

exercises.prompt: A monk starts up a mountain path at 6 a.m. and reaches the temple at the top by 6 p.m., walking at varying speeds and resting often. The next day he leaves the temple at 6 a.m. and walks back down the same path, arriving at the bottom by 6 p.m., again at irregular speeds. Is there definitely some spot on the path that he passes at exactly the same time of day on both days?
choices: Only if he walks at a constant speed both days
Only if both trips take exactly the same time
exercises.explanation: Picture both days happening at once: one monk walking up while a copy walks down. They must meet somewhere on the path, and where they meet is a spot he reaches at the same time on both days. (This is the intermediate value theorem.)

exercises.prompt: What number comes next in this sequence? It only uses the whole numbers one to ten. $$8,\ 5,\ 4,\ 9,\ 1,\ 7,\ 6,\ ?$$
exercises.explanation: These are the numbers one to ten in alphabetical order of their English names: eight, five, four, nine, one, seven, six, then ten (before three and two).
